Infirmier(ère) auxiliaire – Médecine / Courte durée à Chibougamau | Baie-James
 Services SFT est une agence de placement de premier plan spécialisée dans le déploiement de professionnels de la santé partout au Québec. Nous accompagnons les établissements du réseau public dans la couverture de leurs besoins en main-d'œuvre indépendante, tout en offrant à nos candidats des opportunités de carrière uniques, stables et hautement valorisées.
 Nous recherchons actuellement une Infirmière auxiliaire ou un Infirmier auxiliaire pour combler un mandat de longue durée en soins aigus.
 Description du poste
 Joignez-vous à l'équipe de la Direction des soins infirmiers (DSI) au Centre de santé de Chibougamau . Intégré(e) au département de Médecine / Courte durée , vous assurerez la prise en charge, le suivi clinique et la dispensation des soins de santé auprès de patients hospitalisés en phase active.
 Détails du mandat : 
 Période du besoin : Du 11 novembre 2026 au 14 mars 2027 (Mandat de 4 mois).
 Quarts de travail : Flexibilité requise sur les quarts de Jour, Soir et Nuit .
 Type d'horaire : Horaires flexibles de 8 heures, 12 heures ou 16 heures selon les besoins de l'établissement.
 Temps de repas : 45 minutes pour les quarts de 8 heures | 1h40 pour les quarts de 12 heures.
 Horaire atypique : Non.
 Garde (On-Call) : Non.
 Orientation : Une période d'orientation est requise et entièrement planifiée à votre arrivée.
 Vos responsabilités
 Collaborer avec l'équipe multidisciplinaire pour offrir des soins infirmiers de qualité aux patients de l'unité de médecine et courte durée.
 Évaluer l'état de santé des patients, surveiller les signes vitaux et déceler les changements cliniques.
 Participer activement à la surveillance cardiologique (arythmie) et à l'administration sécuritaire de la médication selon votre champ de pratique.
 Assurer la tenue rigoureuse des dossiers cliniques et participer aux transmissions inter-quarts.
 Profil recherché
 Ordre professionnel : Membre en règle et inscription valide au tableau de l' Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers auxiliaires du Québec (OIIAQ) .
 Expérience exigée : Minimum de 2 ans d'expérience consolidée en médecine active .
 Formations spécifiques : Avoir complété avec succès le cours d'arythmie ( Strictement obligatoire ).
 Exigences logistiques : Aucun permis de conduire ni véhicule automobile n'est requis pour ce mandat.
 Aptitudes : Rigueur professionnelle, grande capacité d’adaptation aux horaires variables, esprit d'équipe et excellente gestion du stress en milieu de courte durée.
 Avantages:
 Un accompagnement personnalisé par l'équipe des Normes SFT durant toute la durée de votre assignation.
 Un mandat de longue durée offrant une excellente stabilité professionnelle pour la saison hivernale.
 Une rémunération très compétitive selon les barèmes de main-d'œuvre indépendante de Services SFT.
 Taux horaire 45$/H et 50$/jour travaillé.
 Intéressé(e) ? 
 Envoyez votre CV à jour à :
 info.sft@sftechniques.com 
 Vous pouvez également nous contacter au (438) 946-6340 .
 Notre équipe se fera un plaisir de répondre à toutes vos questions.

Senior Geotechnical Engineer | Tailings & Mine Waste | P.Eng
 We are seeking an accomplished Senior Geotechnical Engineer – Tailings & Mine Waste to join our growing Tailings & Mine Waste team .  Our team delivers engineering and consulting services for tailings storage facilities, mine-waste facilities, waste rock facilities, and related mining infrastructure, supporting clients through investigation, design, construction, operation, monitoring, and closure. This is an opportunity to contribute to complex projects while working alongside experienced engineers and multidisciplinary teams.
 Why Join Equilibrium? 
 Global reach. Specialist expertise. Real influence. 
 Equilibrium brings together the global reach and expertise of an established consultancy with the autonomy and agility of a specialist firm.
 Here, you’ll work closely with experienced leaders, have a genuine voice in the business and see the impact of your work firsthand. As we grow, you’ll have the opportunity to take ownership, deepen your expertise in geotechnical engineering and mine waste, and play a meaningful role in shaping what comes next.
 We want our people to grow with the business, build meaningful relationships and make a lasting contribution - not simply be part of the team, but help build the future of Equilibrium.
 The Role: 
 As a Senior Geotechnical Engineer, Tailings & Mine Waste , you’ll deliver complex tailings and mine waste projects, provide technical guidance, and work closely with clients and multidisciplinary teams. You’ll have the opportunity to apply your technical expertise across investigations, design, and facility assessments, mentor developing engineers, and contribute to the continued growth of Equilibrium’s Mine Waste practice.
 You will:
 Deliver Technical Projects: Manage geotechnical investigations, assessments, and designs for tailings, waste rock spoils and other mine waste facilities, confirming safe work practices, schedule, budget, and client requirements are met.
 Perform Technical Analysis: Perform, oversee, and review geotechnical analyses, interpret field and monitoring data, develop geotechnical models, and provide practical, risk-informed engineering recommendations.
 Support Field Activities: Plan and coordinate geotechnical investigations, inspections, and construction support activities, providing safety oversight, technical direction and responding to site conditions and emerging project requirements.
 Provide Technical Review: Prepare and review engineering reports, calculations, specifications, and technical documentation, while supporting technical reviews, dam safety assessments, risk evaluations, and quality assurance and quality control.
 Support Clients & Project Delivery: Serve as a point of contact for assigned scopes, communicate project status, technical findings and recommendations, and contribute to project planning, proposals, schedules, budgets, and client meetings.
 Develop People: Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and review to junior engineers, engineers-in-training, technologists, and field staff, supporting their professional development.
 Drive Technical Excellence: Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and contribute to continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, industry best practices, and the development of tools, workflows, and quality practices within the Mine Waste practice.
 What We’re Looking For: 
 7 - 10 years of relevant experience in geotechnical engineering, mining, engineering consulting, mine waste, tailings, or project delivery.
 Demonstrated experience in geotechnical design and evaluation of tailings dams, waste rock spoils, and/or co-management structures.
 Demonstrated commitment to health and safety, with experience identifying and managing risks in mine site, field, and project environments. Dam Safety experience considered an asset.
 Strong technical judgement, leadership and project coordination skills.
 Strong interpersonal and emotional intelligence, with the ability to communicate thoughtfully, build trust, provide constructive technical feedback, and navigate challenging situations with empathy.
 Experience contributing to business development, cross-selling, and building long-term client relationships.
 Willingness to travel to mine sites as required.
 Education & Certifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Geological, or related discipline).
 Professional Engineering designation (P.Eng.) or equivalent professional registration required where applicable.
 About Equilibrium: 
 Complex challenges. Practical solutions. Technical excellence. 
 Equilibrium is a specialist technical consultancy serving the global mining and natural resources sectors. We bring together expertise in geotechnical engineering, structural geology, and hydrogeology, to solve complex technical challenges and deliver practical solutions for our clients.
 Founded by internationally respected technical leaders, we combine deep technical expertise with a practical, solutions-focused approach and close client relationships. Our multidisciplinary teams work across regions and disciplines to deliver work that is technically sound, practical and fit for purpose.
 Technical excellence is at the heart of what we do. We are committed to continuously improving our expertise, how we work and the value we deliver to our clients.
 Our People & Culture: 
 Different perspectives make us stronger. 
 We believe bringing together different experiences and ways of thinking makes our teams stronger and our work better. More than half of our team are women, reflecting the inclusive and collaborative culture we are building at Equilibrium.
 We look for people who are technically excellent, curious, empathetic and generous with their knowledge. Initiative, collaboration and fresh thinking shape how we work, while respect and transparency guide how we work with one another.
 We want people to feel heard, supported and empowered to contribute — whether that's sharing an idea, challenging an assumption or helping a colleague succeed.
 Our values — excellence, transparency, diversity and mindfulness of our impact — guide how we work with each other, serve our clients and contribute to our communities and the planet. 
 Compensation: 
 We expect that the salary package to be in the below range depending on experience, qualifications, and skills. The final compensation package will be determined based on the successful candidate’s background and fit for the role.
 $120,000 to $145,000 CAD per year + Benefits + Bonus
 Location: 
 Equilibrium operates globally, with offices in South Brisbane, Australia; Vancouver, Canada; and Portland and Phoenix, USA. 
 We are primarily accepting applications from candidates from within Canada.  Flexible hybrid and remote-based arrangements will be considered for the right individual, depending on location and project requirements. 
 Additional Requirements: 
 Must be legally authorized to work in the country where the position is based. 
 Periodic domestic and/or international travel may be required for project assignments, meetings, training, client engagements, field investigations, and other business purposes, including travel to remote project and mine sites.
 As the Employer operates globally, flexibility in work schedule may be required to support collaboration across different time zones.
 Depending on project or client requirements, the role may require security, background, criminal record, drug and alcohol, or other screening.

Who we are: 
 At Upper Canada Forest Products, we’re more than a leading North American distributor of specialty wood products—we’re a team committed to professionalism, care, and creating spaces that enhance lives and the health of the planet. Founded on the principles of integrity and belonging, we’ve built an organization where your contributions truly matter. 
 Position: Purchaser
 Location: Mississauga, ON
 Employment Type: Full-time, Onsite 
 Vacancy: This posting is for an existing, currently open position. 
 Compensation: $75,000-85,000/yr
 Deliver the Difference with Us:  
 As a Purchaser, you will help ensure the right products are available at the right time, quality and cost to support our customers and branch operations. You will build trusted supplier relationships, make informed purchasing decisions and collaborate closely with sales, operations, warehouse and finance teams. Your work will directly support inventory quality, service levels, margin performance and responsible growth. 
 Your Role and Impact:  
 Reporting to the Purchasing Manager, the Purchaser will manage day-to-day purchasing activities for assigned product categories and suppliers. This role combines supplier management, inventory planning, market awareness, purchase-order execution and analytical follow-through. The successful candidate will be commercially minded, detail oriented and comfortable working independently in a highly collaborative, fast-paced distribution environment. 
 Responsibilities: 
 Review purchase orders for accuracy, authorization and compliance with company policies and agreed supplier terms. 
 Plan and place purchase orders based on demand, inventory targets, lead times, customer requirements and branch priorities. 
 Monitor inventory levels, product availability, open orders, aging inventory and potential stock risks; recommend timely corrective action. 
 Partner with sales and operations to align purchasing decisions with forecasts, customer demand and service expectations. 
 Develop and maintain strong, professional relationships with domestic and global suppliers. 
 Maintain accurate item, supplier, pricing, lead-time and purchase-order information in the ERP system. 
 Analyze purchasing variances, landed costs, market changes and inventory trends; provide clear reports and recommendations to leadership. 
 Identify opportunities to reduce excess and aging inventory, improve inventory turns and strengthen purchasing processes. 
 Collaborate with finance on invoices, credits, cost discrepancies and supplier account issues. 
 Evaluate suppliers based on product quality, pricing, capacity, reliability, service, lead times and alignment with responsible sourcing expectations. 
 Negotiate pricing, freight, terms and other commercial conditions while protecting service, quality and sustainable margin performance. 
 Track supplier performance and resolve cost, quality, delivery, documentation and availability issues promptly. 
 Stay informed about product, supplier, freight, currency and market conditions that may affect availability or cost. 
 Support continuous improvement initiatives and other purchasing or inventory projects as assigned. 
 What Makes You Stand Out: 
 Post-secondary education in business, supply chain, materials management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. 
 Experience in purchasing, procurement, inventory planning or supply chain, preferably in distribution, building materials, forest products or a related product-based environment. 
 Strong commercial judgment, negotiation skills and financial acumen, with an understanding of cost, margin and inventory impacts. 
 Demonstrated ability to analyze data, manage competing priorities and make timely, well-supported decisions. 
 Experience working with ERP or inventory management systems; familiarity with MRP concepts is an asset. 
 Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office skills. 
 Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across suppliers and internal teams. 
 High attention to detail, follow-through and accountability. 
 Knowledge of specialty wood products, lumber, panels, decorative surfaces or related building materials is an asset. 
 Supply chain or procurement designation is an asset. 
 Experience with trucking and logistics an asset.
 Why Join Upper Canada Forest Products? 
 People First Culture: We stand proudly for our people, supporting success through career advancement, continuous learning, and a collaborative environment.
 Competitive Rewards: Enjoy competitive pay, comprehensive family benefits, tuition reimbursement, and programs designed to support not only you but your family as well.
 Growth & Innovation: Join a company that champions innovation and sustainability—where your ideas drive progress and help shape the future.
 Purpose-Driven Work: Our mission is simple: Deliver the Difference to our customers when they need it, by people who know and care. Every role here makes a real impact on our customers and local communities.

 Posting Information:
 This posting is for an existing vacancy.

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose 
 Reporting to the Executive Director, Facilities, the Director, Energy & Mechanical Operations provides leadership and operational oversight for the University of Waterloo’s Mechanical, Electrical and HVAC and Controls building infrastructure teams to ensure safe and reliable day to day operations. In addition, this role is also responsible for the universities energy management programs and storm water management systems across the campus.  This includes ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of campus utilities while advancing energy conservation initiatives that support the University’s sustainability goals.
 The Director leads the planning and management of utility infrastructure operations, supports long-term renewal planning for energy systems, and works collaboratively across Facilities and campus partners to optimize energy performance and system reliability.
 University of Waterloo infrastructure supports more than eight million square feet of academic, research, and administrative space across multiple campuses. The associated energy systems are critical to maintaining safe and effective teaching, research, and campus operations. The Director works in close partnership with the Chief Stationary Engineer to ensure that energy and utility systems are planned, resourced, and operated in alignment with institutional priorities, regulatory requirements, and long‑term infrastructure strategies.
 This role contributes to the Plant Operations goal of providing a safe, reliable, accessible, and well-maintained campus environment through service excellence, operational efficiency, and responsible stewardship of energy resources.
 Key Accountabilities 
 Strategic Planning 
 Acts as the subject matter expert and ensures implementation of the Deferred Capital Renewal plan for energy utility and building systems, ensuring alignment with the University’s long-term academic, research, and campus growth objectives.
 Establishes long-term strategies for the capacity, reliability, and resilience of campus energy infrastructure, including district energy systems, electrical distribution, and utility supply.
 Identifies and prioritizes infrastructure renewal and modernization initiatives related to energy and core building systems to mitigate risks associated with aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance.
 Provides strategic advice to the Executive Director, Facilities and senior leadership regarding long-term utility infrastructure requirements, emerging technologies, and infrastructure risks.
 Directs the development of long-range infrastructure investment plans, balancing operational needs, sustainability commitments, and available funding.
 Develops performance indicators and analytical frameworks to support data-driven decision-making related to infrastructure performance, asset lifecycle management, and system reliability.
 Monitors external trends including energy markets, regulatory changes, and technological advancements and assesses their potential impact on campus infrastructure planning.
 Works collaboratively with the Chief Stationary Engineer to align utility and energy infrastructure planning, performance objectives, and renewal priorities within Central Plants operating capabilities and constraints.
 Partners with the Chief Stationary Engineer to assess operational risks, system reliability trends, and capacity limitations, and to develop mitigation and investment strategies.
 Energy Management 
 Leads the University of Waterloo’s Energy Management program, identifying and implementing initiatives to improve energy efficiency and reduce institutional energy consumption.
 Works collaboratively with the Sustainability Office and campus partners to support the University’s sustainability goals.
 Provides technical expertise to the Executive Director, Facilities on matters related to energy consumption, utility supply, sustainability initiatives, and energy efficiency opportunities.
 Oversees development of multi-year utility forecasts, incorporating projected consumption, regulatory changes, and energy market conditions.
 Directs the evaluation of campus energy systems to identify energy conservation opportunities and operational improvements.
 Oversees the development of business cases, funding proposals, and external submissions related to energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives.
 Provides oversight to the Energy Manager in the negotiation and management of utility supply contracts and agreements.
 Collaborates with faculty, staff, and students on the implementation of energy reduction initiatives, ensuring alignment with the University’s academic and research mission.
 Infrastructure Renewal 
 Contributes to capital planning and infrastructure renewal planning related to energy, utility and building systems.
 Provides technical input into the prioritization of deferred maintenance and system renewal initiatives affecting campus energy infrastructure.
 Supports development of business cases and capital funding requests for infrastructure renewal and modernization projects.
 Collaborates with the Design and Construction team to ensure projects involving utility infrastructure are effectively coordinated.
 Works with campus partners to identify opportunities to improve energy performance, operational efficiency, and infrastructure resiliency.
 Project Management and Procurement 
 Provides oversight to staff managing energy and utility infrastructure projects, including system upgrades and efficiency initiatives.
 Ensures projects are delivered in accordance with University procurement policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
 Supports project planning and implementation while ensuring adherence to health and safety standards and construction regulations.
 Financial Management 
 Develops and manages the operating budget for energy management programs.
 Monitors utility costs and operational expenditures and identifies opportunities for efficiency and cost optimization.
 Identifies opportunities for operational efficiencies and cost optimization.
 Contributes to the development of capital budget requests related to energy and utility infrastructure renewal.
 Ensures appropriate financial tracking and reporting for projects and operational activities.
 People Leadership 
 Provides leadership, mentorship, and strategic direction to managers, supervisors, and technical staff within the Energy Management team.
 Oversees performance planning and review processes for direct reports and ensures consistent leadership practices across operational teams.

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Why we're looking for you



At Owner, authentication and authorization sit at the center of trust. Every restaurant owner, employee, partner, and internal teammate depends on secure, reliable access to the right tools at the right time — whether they’re ringing up orders, balancing the books, or supporting customers behind the scenes.



We’re building the next generation of our identity and access platform, and we need an exceptional engineer to help us get there. You’ll join a small, high-trust team with direct ownership over login, session management, permissions, roles, service-to-service auth, and the APIs and infrastructure every product team at Owner builds on top of. This is a rare opportunity to shape a foundational security platform at a fast-growing company — one that has to scale with our product surface, our customer base, and the complexity of the restaurants we serve.



This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada.



The impact you'll have



 - Help build the foundation for secure access at Owner — design and improve the authentication and authorization systems that power every product surface across the platform.

 - Own critical auth infrastructure end to end — contribute to systems for login, sessions, token management, service-to-service auth, account security, and access enforcement.

 - Improve reliability and observability — instrument auth services with the alerting, dashboards, and runbooks needed to detect issues quickly and keep critical access flows healthy.

 - Raise the security bar — identify risks, improve controls, and help ensure authentication and authorization are designed thoughtfully from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

 - Leverage AI tools to move faster — use AI tooling to accelerate your work, from writing and reviewing code to exploring solutions and automating repetitive tasks.

 - Help us build a great team — interview candidates, share technical context, and raise the bar for how we build.



Who you’ll work with



 - A small, focused authentication and authorization team — you’ll work closely with a tight-knit group of engineers who own identity and access end to end.

 - Engineers across product, platform, infrastructure, and security — auth is a foundation every team depends on, so you’ll partner closely on APIs, access patterns, and implementation standards.

 - Product and Design — to ensure access flows are secure, intuitive, and aligned with the needs of restaurants and internal teams.



Minimum requirements



 - 8+ years of experience building and shipping production backend systems, with a track record of owning critical services end to end — not just contributing to them.

 - Comfort with Typescript or Javascript — with deep experience in building web-scale applications.

 - Hands-on experience building authentication, authorization, identity, permissions, security, or similar platform infrastructure.

 - Strong understanding of API design, distributed systems, databases, and operational reliability.

 - Strong sense of ownership and urgency — you don’t wait for perfect requirements, you drive toward clarity and keep things moving.



Compensation and benefits

 

 - The estimated starting base salary range for this role is $220K-$240K depending on level, location and experience, plus a generous pre-IPO equity package

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, work from anywhere (remote-first workplace), unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

ARE YOU A SOFTWARE DEVELOPER WITH A PASSION FOR FINDING CREATIVE SOLUTIONS TO REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS? 

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for an Intermediate Software Engineer to be part of our Software Engineering team.

At Jobber, we don’t just build a product - we work on real problems that help people in small businesses to become successful. We are inspired by our company values: be humble, be supportive and give a sh*t, which are not just said but are lived. We work in a collaborative environment where teams make decisions with autonomy and contribute directly to shaping the company’s future. We release early and often while dedicating time to addressing technical debt. We believe in getting instant feedback from our customers and leveraging that to make their lives easier.

We help employees grow professionally; we have a ton of onboarding resources, tutorials, hackathons, and buddies to support learnings and provide opportunities to innovate. We have a range of experience levels on teams which allow for mentor/mentee opportunities. Leaders at Jobber work with empathy and support employees to build a healthy work-life harmony. Bring your dedication and passion to this job to fulfill your goals.

You could join one of the following teams:

AI Foundations: AI Foundations is responsible for all the underlying tooling and infrastructure to enable teams create and scale AI-powered experiences in Jobber. This is a backend-heavy team working primarily in Rails and Node with an emphasis on supporting and enabling other Jobber feature teams to build high-quality, efficient, and scalable AI-powered experiences.

The role:

Reporting to the Manager, Software Engineering, the Intermediate Software Engineer will collaborate with other Software Development members on a Scrum team to build an industry-leading product that helps our customers and their small businesses be successful. We’re looking for people who are ready to solve problems that millions of entrepreneurs are facing and who are eager to develop their craft while contributing to the team’s success.

In this role, you must be committed to writing well-tested, scalable, and well-organized code. In addition, you will customize, extend and experiment with tools, models, harnesses and processes to increase your effectiveness. You’ll have opportunities to learn, collaborate, and grow while supporting your team in delivering high-quality solutions.



As an Intermediate Software Engineer, you will:

 - Contribute to the design, development, and delivery of features that address customer needs, collaborating with cross-functional teams

 - Work closely with senior engineers to refine requirements and scope technical solutions.

 - Write, review, and maintain clean, scalable, and well-documented code.

 - Participate in code reviews to ensure code quality and maintainability.

 - Collaborate with your team to identify and solve technical challenges.

 - Share knowledge and learn from others through paired programming, team discussions, and technical documentation.

 - Stay curious and keep up to date with the latest tools, technologies, and best practices in software development.

 - Build with AI as a core part of how you work. We expect engineers to delegate real work to agents daily, verify what comes back, and keep improving their own setup so each task makes the next one easier.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Proficiency in writing clean, maintainable, and testable code.

 - Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies.

 - A structured understanding of common backend frameworks, technologies, and patterns.

 - Familiarity working with observability tools such as DataDog.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and a collaborative mindset.

 - A willingness to learn, adapt, and grow as part of a team.

 - Daily hands-on experience building with agentic AI tools, beyond autocomplete or chat: you delegate real work to agents as part of how you ship.

It would be great (but not a deal-breaker) if you had:

 - Experience with our development stack: React, React Native, TypeScript, Ruby on Rails 

 - Familiarity with GraphQL API Layer and its optimization.

 - Prior experience working on scalable distributed systems.

 - Exposure to background processing frameworks (e.g., Sidekiq, Active Jobs).

Hiring Process:

 - An interview with a Talent team member (45 mins)

 - A Hiring Manager Interview (60 mins),

 -  A take-home challenge with a follow-up Functional Interview (90 mins), 

 - A Senior Leadership Interview (30 mins). 
   

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.


Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $106,600, a midpoint of $125,400, and a maximum salary of $144,200, designed to reflect the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling. 

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience, and the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth. 

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development. We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.




OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 

Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.




AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an outstanding Analyst to join a team that’s building the best corporate card and spend management platform in Canada.



In this role, you’ll be responsible for ‘diligencing’, analyzing, and driving the growth of Float’s credit portfolio.





WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Conducting thorough, and efficient, analyses of business fundamentals and financial performance for Float’s potential and existing credit investments, ranging from VC backed growth companies to longstanding, profitable Canadian businesses

 - Monitoring the performance of Float’s credit portfolio, tracking account behaviour, and proactively identifying signs of potential credit deterioration.

 - Conducting periodic financial reviews of existing clients, analyzing business fundamentals, financial health, and repayment capacity.

 - Assessing credit exposures relative to limits, recommending adjustments where necessary, and escalating concerns to the Credit Committee.

 - Collaborating with clients to gather updated financial information and address inquiries, balancing risk management with customer experience.

 - Supporting the continuous improvement of Float’s credit monitoring framework, risk policies, and portfolio management practices.

 - Participating in due diligence calls with executives (CFO, CEO, VP Finance and Controller)

 - Partnering with our Sales & Marketing and Customer Success teams to relay feedback on what types of opportunities are adding the most value to Float

 - Using our portfolio performance data to derive insights on how we can grow and shape the portfolio for optimal impact



In addition to living our values…

 - You love investing. To be successful in this role, you’ll need to have a love of investing. The analysis you’ll be conducting is similar to how a private debt or equity fund would think about its investments.

 - You’ve got the experience. To be successful in this role, we’re looking for 2+ years of accounting, transaction advisory, consulting, corporate or investment banking, or other similar experience, ideally with a bachelor’s degree (though that’s not required)

 - You relate to people extremely well. While you need to search deeply for the right answers, you’ll need the ability to do so in a way that partners with our prospects collaboratively to uncover the truth, vs. doing so confrontationally.

 - You think critically. You don’t just take others’ opinions for granted; you truth seek to validate or disprove investment hypotheses.

 - You’re conscientious. You make few mistakes in calculations or otherwise. Even while being creative and taking risks to find the best due diligence approach, you are extremely thorough and meticulous in the way you go about your work.

 - You’ve got an understanding of the market. You’re commercially focused with an understanding of the market and the business we’re in and have an ROI mindset.

 - You’re eager to continue your own learning. Scrappy and voracious, you want to know the ‘why’ behind every answer. You’re a thinker who can combine quantitative thinking with qualitative judgment.

 - You’re skilled at analyzing data to uncover insights and trends that inform investment decisions. Familiarity with SQL or similar tools is a plus.

 - Bonus, but not required: You also speak French to be able to communicate with Quebec-based prospects and executives.



This may not be the role for you if...

 - You need close day-to-day direction rather than working independently

 - You’re not energized by feedback or fast-paced change

 - You’re seeking predictability over adaptability

 - You’re not comfortable making decisions in ambiguous situations

 - You prefer to stay in your lane rather than collaborate cross-functionally

 - You don’t feel a strong connection to Float’s mission or the product we’re building




OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

We hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Titles matter less than impact, and every hire is expected to raise the bar for Float as a whole.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

 - Work at one of Canada's fastest-growing fintech companies

 - Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role

 - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team

 - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits

 - Hybrid work model – we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration

 - Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday

 - Bring your pup to our dog-friendly office

 - Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters




IN SHORT

At Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special—and having a lot of fun along the way. If you’re excited to build, grow, and win together, we’d love to meet you.

 

We’re committed to building a workplace that’s welcoming and accessible for everyone. If you need any accommodations during the hiring process or once you join Float, just let us know! You can reach out to Vic https://www.linkedin.com/in/victoria-boult-b21b2053/ (victoria@floatfinancial.com), and we’ll work with you to make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Faire face à la crise climatique est une priorité mondiale urgente et nous prenons notre responsabilité très au sérieux. S'appuyant sur plus de 130 ans d'expérience dans la résolution des défis mondiaux, GE Vernova occupe une position unique pour contribuer à la transition énergétique en continuant à électrifier le monde tout en œuvrant simultanément à sa décarbonisation. GE Vernova aide ses clients à réaliser des économies d'énergie et à fournir une électricité vitale pour la santé, la sûreté et l'amélioration de la qualité de vie. GE Vernova a son siège social à Cambridge, dans le Massachusetts, aux États-Unis, et compte plus de 80 000 employés dans plus de 140 pays à travers le monde.
Les turbines et les alternateurs de la division Hydro Power de GE Vernova représentent plus de 25 % de la capacité totale installée dans le monde. Notre portefeuille de solutions pour la production d'énergie hydroélectrique comprend la plus large gamme de solutions et de services hydroélectriques : de l'eau au réseau, des équipements individuels aux solutions clés en main complètes, pour les nouvelles centrales et la base installée. Notre passion pour les solutions de service et de remise à neuf vient compléter ce portefeuille afin de tirer le meilleur parti des équipements de nos clients. L'activité Hydro Power de GE Vernova possède la plus grande base installée d'unités de stockage hydroélectrique en activité. Avec plus de 30 % des centrales de type pompe-turbine du monde équipées de nos technologies et plus de 6 000 MW de projets en cours de développement dans le monde entier, nous sommes en mesure de fournir une solution adaptée aux besoins spécifiques de nos clients dans des environnements variés. La principale mission du groupe calculs spéciaux est de réaliser des études par éléments finis (FEA) afin de valider la résistance mécanique structurale et la résistance en fatigue des composantes turbine et alternateur.
 Poste : 
En tant que stagiaire calculs mécaniques, vous vous joindrez à un environnement dynamique et diversifié faisant partie des équipes de conception mécanique turbines et alternateurs hydroélectriques. Dans ce rôle, vous aurez l'occasion de travailler aux côtés de professionnels expérimentés dans le domaine de l'ingénierie de conception mécanique. Vous allez acquérir une exposition en soutenant les ingénieurs de ces équipes et en aidant l'organisation générale à atteindre ses buts et ses objectifs annuels comme participant actif.
 Nature du travail : 
Les responsabilités de cette fonction comprennent (entre autres) :
 Réaliser des analyses principalement par éléments finis visant à valider la résistance mécanique de composantes turbine et alternateur de machines neuves et réfectionnées.
 Réaliser des analyses de fatigue conformément à la norme ASME.
 Réaliser la validation mécanique des soudures en statique et en fatigue de composants mécanos soudés suivant les codes applicables (CSA W59, AWS D1.1,)
 Apporter son soutien aux autres groupes d'ingénierie pour la réalisation de calculs complémentaires.
 Rédiger des notes de calcul en français et/ou en anglais pour les clients ou les parties prenantes internes
 Participer à la rédaction de guide de conception
 Possédez-vous les compétences requises? Nous recherchons... 
 Habiletés : 
 Individus ayant moins de 2 ans d'expérience de travail (en dehors de co- op / stages / expérience estivale)
 Avoir au moins deux années universitaires complétées en Génie Mécanique ou Aérospatial.
 Connaître les notions de base en analyse par éléments finis.
 Être familier avec la résistance des matériaux ainsi qu'avec la mécanique des fluides et les vibrations.
 Avoir une bonne base des logiciels de bureautique WORD et EXCEL ainsi qu'en conception assistée par ordinateur (CAO).
 Maîtriser l'anglais écrit (anglais oral est un atout).
 Additional Information 
 Relocation Assistance Provided: No

 - Advanced Excel and financial modelling skills

 - Working knowledge of credit facility mechanics: borrowing bases, advance rates, eligibility criteria and payment waterfalls

 - Experience working with large loan-level datasets; SQL or Python is an asset

 - Experience preparing reporting for external parties such as lenders, banks or agents

ABOUT BEACON SOFTWARE:

Beacon https://beaconsoftware.com/ is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.




ROLE AND MISSION:

This is an exciting and entrepreneurial opportunity to join a fast-paced technology company with a very significant growth trajectory. Beacon Software is making its first hire on the Strategic Finance team. This is a role where investing turns into building. The individual will report to Beacon’s VP, Strategic Finance and work closely with Beacon’s CEO, CTO, M&A Directors, industry pod leaders, and the General Managers of Beacon’s portfolio companies.

The Strategic Finance team’s mandate spans the financial decisions that shape Beacon: partnering with portfolio companies on growth and value creation, building AI-native systems that let functions scale non-linearly with the portfolio, owning Beacon’s capital allocation across organic and inorganic strategies, leading new strategy extensions beyond core software M&A, and building Beacon’s capital markets capability. Team members work across a mix of these areas based on their interests and skillset.

This is an asymmetric opportunity to build a company, with decision authority and velocity over process driving compounding equity. You’ll sit next to the CEO on capital allocation and capital markets, or fill a CFO role across dozens of companies on their most consequential decisions. The playbook will be shaped by you with the goal of building Beacon into a $100B company.

To succeed in this role, this individual should be an enthusiastic and energetic self-starter, with the ability to translate operator intuition into financial decisions and build the analytical rigor behind Beacon’s platform-level bets. The ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously across portfolio companies and platform initiatives will be essential. We are seeking a collaborative professional who wants to contribute ideas on how to improve the status quo and create best-practices that will accelerate our execution. Teamwork and positivity are key foundations of this growing team’s culture and ethos.

Location: for discussion. Beacon has offices in Toronto, San Francisco, New York, and Chicago.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Finance partner to acquired companies:

 - Partner with industry sector leaders and portfolio company General Managers as the financial decision-making engine across Beacon’s portfolio companies.

 - Translate product, AI, and operator intuition into investment decisions: pricing changes, sales hires, direct marketing investments, engineering allocation, and tuck-in M&A.

 - Build value creation plans, set budgets and targets, and make the day-to-day capital decisions that drive growth across companies.

Beacon capital allocation:

 - Help own platform-level capital allocation: organic platform investment vs. inorganic M&A, platform-level acquisitions vs. tuck-ins, debt vs. equity at the corporate level.

 - Build the analytical rigor behind Beacon’s platform-level bets, ensuring capital is deployed where returns are most asymmetric.

Strategy extension beyond core software M&A:

 - Own thesis through acquisition through ownership for new strategy extensions, starting with software-plus-services vertical integration in end markets where Beacon already owns software.

 - Partner with the M&A team for execution while driving the strategy, the diligence, and the post-close build.

Capital markets:

 - Lead Beacon’s debt strategy, support future equity raises, and prepare Beacon for an eventual IPO.

 - Build best-in-class debt and equity investor relations and position Beacon as an institutional-grade capital allocator.

Build AI-native finance systems:

 - Partner with Beacon’s CTO and engineering leadership on the company-wide tools that scale across the portfolio, including BeaconOS and AI-native financial systems.

 - Build the systems, dashboards, and decision frameworks that let sector leaders and GMs self-serve the financial answers they need, allowing the finance function to scale non-linearly with the portfolio.




QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 3-8 years of post-undergrad experience in strategy consulting, private equity, or other finance roles (e.g., investment banking, growth equity, corporate development, or strategic finance).

 - Strong academic record from a competitive institution with a degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

 - Investor mindset, analytical toolkit, and operator instinct: equally comfortable building a model and being in the room with a product leader or GM helping them make the call.

 - Expertise in building financial models, value creation plans, and analytical frameworks for capital allocation decisions.

 - Strong ability to synthesize complex systems and communicate clearly to senior stakeholders.

 - Familiarity with vertical market software, buy-and-build models, and the operating dynamics of small-to-mid-sized software businesses is a plus.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with founders, CEOs, GMs, board members, and investors.

 - Ability to translate high-level objectives into actionable work plans and to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

 - High attention to detail combined with the ability to zoom out and see the bigger picture.

 - Demonstrated high agency: comfort building the playbook, not just running it.

 - Curiosity and willingness to use AI tools heavily as part of the day-to-day workflow.

 - Conducts all interactions with a high level of integrity and trust.




WHAT YOU WILL GET FROM BEACON:

 - Direct exposure to M&A, capital markets, AI-native systems, and IPO-grade operations.

 - Network and learn from leading public and private equity investors who are Beacon LPs, including the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp.

 - Attend exclusive Beacon Speaker Series fireside chats with legendary venture capital, private equity, and hedge fund investors as well as eminent technology leaders.

 - Work directly with Silicon Valley product and engineering teams on portfolio value creation and platform technology investments.

 - Compounding equity in a company structured as a permanent capital vehicle, with no pressure to exit.

 - A clear line of sight from your work to enterprise value creation across dozens of operating companies.

 - A unique work environment that combines a high-growth technology startup with a long-term buy-and-hold investment platform.




IDEAL CANDIDATE:

 - Experience working at a top private equity, growth equity, or hedge fund.

 - Experience working at another serial acquirer, especially in software or vertical-market roll-ups.

 - Investment banking experience at a top-tier firm with software, technology, or M&A coverage.

 - Impatient with actions, patient with results

 - Play for front of the jersey

 - Intellectually curious

 - Perpetual learner

 - Low bureaucracy

 - Systems thinker

 - Optimistic

 - Commercial

 - Ambitious


Our Values at Beacon Software

Who We Are 
 SWTCH is pioneering EV charging solutions for multifamily and commercial properties across North America. Since 2016, our team of entrepreneurs, energy professionals, and technologists has been focused on unlocking the social, economic, and environmental benefits of widespread EV adoption. Today, our solutions are deployed in tens of thousands of locations —many of which are low-to-moderate income housing—helping to make clean mobility accessible for all.
 With an expanding footprint across Canada and the U.S., we’re scaling quickly and looking for mission-driven talent to help accelerate our growth.
 The Role 
 At SWTCH, we're accelerating the adoption of electric vehicles by delivering intelligent charging solutions that make EV charging more accessible, reliable, and efficient. Our platform powers thousands of charging stations across North America, helping property owners, businesses, utilities, and drivers transition to a more sustainable future.
 We're looking for a QA Automation Engineer who is passionate about software quality and automation to help ensure our products are reliable, scalable, and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
 The Opportunity
 Today, our automated test coverage is unit tests and some integration testing — we have no systematic automated coverage of end-to-end user flows. That's the gap this role exists to close. You'll design and build our automated E2E testing practice from the ground up, working closely with Product and Engineering to make sure we stop shipping regressions as we scale. You'll have real latitude here: this isn't a role where testing requirements arrive fully formed. Product can tell you what the product needs to do; figuring out how we verify it actually does that reliably is yours to define.
 How We Work
 Decisions live as close to the work as possible — you'll own how testing gets built, not just execute a checklist someone else wrote.
 We're kind, not nice — we say the hard thing early, in a way that respects the person hearing it. Feedback is specific and timely, not saved for a review cycle.
 We ship in small increments and treat real usage as the fastest way to learn what's working.
 We hold strong opinions loosely — bring conviction, stay open to being wrong.
 What you'll be doing 
 Guide Product Managers in translating use cases into testable requirements and edge cases — PMs bring the "what," you bring the "how do we know it actually works."
 Own the definition of test strategy and testing standards, and design our automated E2E / user-flow testing approach from scratch.
 Develop and execute automated functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end test suites.
 Implement the automated portions of the testing plans you define.
 Mentor and train engineers on writing, maintaining, and extending automated tests — part of this role's mandate is building testing capability across the team, not just within QA.
 Perform manual/exploratory testing where automation isn't yet in place.
 Identify, document, and track defects, working with engineering to drive timely resolution.
 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
 Monitor test execution, analyze failures, and continuously improve coverage and reliability.
 What You'll Bring
 5+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, including 3+ years focused on test automation.
 Experience in testing web applications, APIs, mobile apps and backend services.
 Experience designing an automated testing practice from scratch — not just extending one that already exists.
 Comfort partnering with Product Managers who rely on you to help surface testing needs and edge cases
 Hands-on experience with test automation frameworks (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or similar).
 Experience testing REST APIs (Postman or similar).
 Proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript; Ruby experience is a plus given our Rails services.
 Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and Agile practices.
 Experience mentoring or upskilling other engineers in testing practices.
 Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills; excellent communication.
 Nice to Have
 Experience with IoT, connected devices, or hardware-interfacing software — this is the environment you'd be working in day to day, though not a requirement.
 Experience with EV charging, OCPP, or similar device-communication protocols.
 Familiarity with AWS, Azure, or GCP.
 Performance or load testing experience.
 A Note on Our Stack
 We're primarily Python and TypeScript, with React on the frontend and some Ruby on Rails services. We're directionally leaning toward Playwright as our automation framework, but that's not locked in — it's unproven at our scale, and if you've got a strong point of view otherwise, we want to hear it.
 Why Join SWTCH?
 You'll be building something that doesn't exist yet at a company where your judgment on how to build it is genuinely trusted, not just tolerated. If you want ownership over a testing practice from day one — and the chance to shape how an engineering team thinks about quality — we'd love to talk.

 À Aviso, nous nous consacrons à l’amélioration du bien-être financier des Canadiennes et des Canadiens.  L’occasion:

Il s’agit d’une occasion de façonner un domaine très délicat et important de l’expérience du personnel en établissant des cadres, une gouvernance, des flux de travail, un suivi et des rapports évolutifs, tout en veillant à ce que l’administration quotidienne du programme soit effectuée de manière rigoureuse, uniforme et conforme. 
 La personne retenue aura l’occasion de bâtir et d’améliorer l’infrastructure du programme, d’améliorer les processus et la gouvernance, et de fournir des conseils de confiance aux gestionnaires, aux partenaires des RH, aux membres du personnel et aux fournisseurs externes. En travaillant au sein d’une équipe Personnes et culture qui met l’accent sur la collaboration, vous aiderez à créer une expérience plus fluide, conforme et axée sur le personnel pour les personnes qui composent avec des congés, des mesures d’adaptation et la réintégration au travail, tout en veillant à ce que le programme soit maintenu, administré et surveillé efficacement, en plus de faire l’objet d’améliorations continuelles. 
 En tant qu’uneaviso :

 Nous nous surpassons – Vous collaborez ouvertement et établissez des relations significatives. Vous recherchez des points de vue variés, partagez vos connaissances et travaillez de concert avec les collègues, la clientèle et les partenaires pour les aider à réussir. 
 Nous livrons des résultats – Vous assumez la responsabilité de votre travail, respectez vos engagements et vous concentrez sur la production de résultats concrets. Vous êtes responsable de vos actions et cherchez constamment à vous améliorer. 
 À quoi ressemble votre journée: 
 Diriger l’évolution continue du programme d’absences autorisées et de mesures d’adaptation au travail, qui comprendra la recherche d’occasions de moderniser les processus, d’améliorer l’expérience du personnel, de renforcer la gouvernance et d’harmoniser les pratiques avec les objectifs organisationnels.
 Superviser la réception des demandes, la coordination des dossiers, la documentation et la résolution de cas complexes d’absences, d’invalidité et de mesures d’adaptation, notamment la planification du retour au travail et la mise en œuvre de mesures d’adaptations appropriées au lieu de travail.
 Fournir des conseils de spécialiste aux gestionnaires, aux RH et aux membres du personnel sur les droits aux absences, les exigences en matière d’adaptation et les obligations en matière de conformité.
 Fournir des conseils et administrer toutes les absences prévues par la loi, en veillant à ce que les membres du personnel et les gestionnaires reçoivent des directives claires et à ce que les processus relatifs aux absences soient gérés de façon uniforme et conformément aux lois applicables.
 Élaborer et maintenir des politiques, des procédures et des flux de travail pour assurer la prestation uniforme, conforme et efficace du programme.

 Surveiller les activités, les tendances et les résultats du programme, notamment en assumant la responsabilité du suivi des mesures du programme et de la préparation de rapports réguliers pour soutenir la prestation des services, renforcer la gouvernance et améliorer l’expérience du personnel.

You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels: 
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own.
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 You’re people-smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of Team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter.
 Please read carefully: 
 1. Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What’s the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job:
 If you don’t have one, explain why.
 If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Show us what you’ve done.
 Please include links to social accounts, campaigns, posts, videos, or other work you’ve helped create or manage.
 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.
 4. Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best — and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume. 
 Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read! 
 We’re looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly and you can expect a prompt response.

About Gusto 
 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.
 About the Role: 
 Gusto is looking for a VC & PE Partnerships Manager to own and scale our relationships across venture capital (VC) and private equity (PE) firms.
 This role sits at the intersection of partnerships, investing, and go-to-market strategy. You’ll own how Gusto engages with the investor ecosystem in a way that is thoughtful, scalable, and aligned with long-term business priorities, and you’ll be accountable for the results of that motion across the function. Rather than managing a broad set of one-off relationships, this role focuses on building high-leverage, programmatic ecosystem partnerships that consistently show up early in a founder’s journey.
 You’ll partner closely with teams across various Partnerships teams, Marketing, Events, and Sales to define the right portfolio, engagement model, and success metrics for this motion.
 About the Team: 
 The Channel Partnerships function sits within Gusto’s broader Partnerships organization. We work cross-functionally to extend Gusto’s reach through trusted partners, while ensuring our motions scale sustainably over time. This team acts as a connective layer between the startup ecosystem and Gusto’s go-to-market engine—balancing long-term relationship building with clear ownership, guardrails, and outcomes.
 Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: 
 Own Gusto’s VC & PE partnership strategy end to end, accountable for results across the function
 Define and maintain a clear partner portfolio, including which partners warrant 1:1 investment versus scaled engagement
 Build repeatable, programmatic partnership motions (e.g., portfolio company programs, founder and operator education, marketplace or platform integrations)
 Serve as the Tier 1 point of contact for a core group of high-impact ecosystem partners
 Collaborate closely with Partner Marketing and Events to design scalable programs and moments of engagement
 Partner with Recruit and other internal teams to align on net-new partner sourcing over time
 Track and evaluate ecosystem impact across metrics such as ARR, pipeline influence, and founder reach
 Represent Gusto externally as a credible, recognized voice in the VC & PE ecosystem, and provide thought leadership to internal teams and external partners
 Here’s what we're looking for: 
 5+ years of experience in partnerships, ecosystem development, venture or growth programs, or adjacent roles, with a track record of function-level impact
 3+ years of experience with the venture capital and private equity ecosystem , including founders, operators, and investors
 Proven ability to independently lead complex, cross-functional partnership initiatives that balance relationship depth with scalability
 Strong judgment around where to invest time and where to say “not now”
 Comfort working cross-functionally and influencing without direct authority
 Ability to translate ambiguous inputs into clear strategy and execution plans
 Experience working at or closely with a VC or PE firm, high-growth company, or ecosystem platform
 Background in program design, portfolio engagement, or platform partnerships
 Experience evaluating partnership impact beyond direct revenue attribution
 Our cash compensation amount for this role is $153,000 to $195,000 USD for Denver, Phoenix, Atlanta metro areas and $180,815 to $230,000 USD for San Francisco & New York and $146,940-$185,000 CAD for Toronto. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above. 
 At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.
 Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.
 Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.
